summary.headline: Rikhav Securities FY26 PAT about ₹19 crore on total income about ₹191.6 crore; transcript is an AGM, not a Q2 FY27 call.
summary.overview: This transcript is of the 31st AGM held September 22, 2026, not a Q2 FY27 earnings call, though the filing is labelled as an analyst/investor meet outcome dated 2026-11-06. Management described FY26 as a challenging year with moderated market participation, losses on older capital market positions, and higher depreciation from technology investment. The chairman's speech cited total income of about ₹191.6 crore and PAT of about ₹19 crore, with a growth figure of about 45.5% that is unclear in the transcript. The rest of the meeting covered routine resolutions: adoption of FY26 financial statements and reappointment of a director. The transcript is auto-generated and heavily garbled, so figures should be verified against the annual report.

segments.name: Broking / capital markets
segments.commentary: Management said it is reducing reliance on market-linked income and shifting to recurring streams across proprietary trading, margin trading facility (MTF), market making, SME services and institutional business. Market making spans NSE and BSE SME platforms; over 46 SME listings supported annually, per transcript.

guidance_outlook: Management said the business mix is evolving toward higher-quality fee-based and interest-based income, but gave no numeric guidance.
Plans to expand institutional business with banks and foreign institutional investors, and to grow through sub-broker and franchise networks with limited fixed-cost increase.
Next phase of growth to be shaped by disciplined capital allocation, continued technology and automation investment, and a more diversified model.
capex_capacity: Invested about ₹5 crore (as transcribed, 'approximately five') in software and technology enhancement during FY26, covering trading infrastructure, operational scalability and back-office efficiency.
Upgraded mobile trading platform, eKYC system for faster onboarding, real-time multi-asset market access and automated risk management framework.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian broking and capital market participation moderated across several segments in FY26, with rapid market changes reducing the effectiveness of some trading opportunities.
Broking margins described as modest given high volumes in a competitive environment.
Serves over 23,000 clients, with a stated 99% (figure garbled) retention or continuity; no pricing data disclosed.
risks_watch: Losses on certain older capital market positions weighed on FY26 profit; amount not stated in transcript.
Higher depreciation from technology investment will continue to weigh on margins.
Market-linked revenue remains a large share of income, and management is trying to reduce it.

summary.management_tone: Measured and candid: management openly acknowledged FY26 headwinds, losses and margin pressure, while stressing long-term conviction in capital-market growth and a shift to recurring revenue. No Q&A session took place, so there were no evasive answers.
